hero.title: Dirty truth or dare, the version that holds nothing back
hero.description: 70 cards for two, from suggestive to very direct, on a single phone and with nothing to prepare.

section1.title: One deck that runs from suggestive to very direct
section1.p1: A dirty truth or dare that starts too strong does not work: the first dare makes someone uncomfortable and the game ends before it began. That is why this deck builds up rather than hitting hard from the start.
section1.p2: The gentlest cards stay suggestive: questions that make you blush, dares that bring you closer, nothing that forces anyone to undress. The most direct ones drop the precautions and assume you both know where you are going. The draw mixes them, and the right to pass is what keeps you in control.
section1.p3: Start gently even if you think you can skip a step. The laughter of the early cards does more for the rest of the evening than any dare thrown in cold.

section2.title: How it is played
section2.intro: The rules are the same as the classic version, with one extra point that matters more here.
section2.regle1Texte: The game announces whose turn it is on every card, so nobody has to argue about who plays next.
section2.regle2Texte: The player called out picks their side, and the card is drawn at random from the matching deck. You never see the next one.
section2.regle3Titre: Passing is built into the game
section2.regle3Texte: Turning a card down brings a forfeit, and that is all. It is the most important rule in this version: it makes refusing ordinary instead of an admission.
section2.regle4Titre: You set the limit, not the game
section2.regle4Texte: Decide before you start what is off the table tonight. A game never replaces an agreement between the two of you, it only makes suggestions.

section3.title: Consent, said simply
section3.p1: This game suggests, it imposes nothing. Every card can be refused without explanation, as many times as needed, and a forfeit is never a punishment to endure. If one of you is not in the mood, the right answer is to stop the game, not to negotiate.
section3.p2: The cards are written for a couple playing together, between consenting adults. They assume you know each other and that you both know when to stop.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: How is it different from the classic version?
faq.a1: The cards. The classic version is for every couple and can be played in front of anyone. This one has its own deck, far more direct, written for a moment when it is just the two of you.
faq.a2: It runs from suggestive to very direct. The gentlest cards ask for a compliment or a kiss, the most direct ones assume an intimacy already in place. There is no level to pick: the right to pass is what sets the limit, card by card.
faq.a3: 70 in total: 30 truths, 24 dares and 16 forfeits, all in one deck. They do not repeat until the deck runs out, which is enough for a whole evening without landing on the same ones.
faq.q4: Is it suitable for a couple who have just met?
faq.a4: The gentler end of the deck, yes, it works well for testing the water. The most direct cards assume you already know each other well: if one lands too early, pass, that is exactly what it is there for.
faq.a5: No, and nothing is recorded. The game runs in your browser, your answers never leave the device and there is no game history.

section4.title: What a game like this can really do
section4.p1: It is not going to transform your intimate life, and nobody should ask it to. What it does well is give a frame to a conversation many couples have never really had, because the card asks the question for you.
section4.p2: The rest is yours to decide, and that is exactly as it should be.
